summary: Implemented four of five plan phases cleanly and committed each separately: a leaked-fixture reaper pass in claude-refresh.sh with fixture-driven test coverage (Phase 1), a 1,493-entry/~851MB /tmp backlog reclamation (Phase 2), a --corpus-probe suppression guard in verify-deploy.sh saving ~2.4s per gate-narrowed invocation (Phase 3), and a standing specs/decisions/ verdict record carrying the 0-DELETE/14-KEEP verdict, the four-way suite-population counting methodology, and the demotion-tier non-recommendation (Phase 5). Phase 4 (re-measure gate-cost-model.csv/suite-cost-hints.txt) closed [PARTIAL]: host load rose to 3.26-3.86 (above measure-gate-costs.sh's 2.0 threshold) partway through its own measurement pass -- a contaminated cost artifact is worse than a stale one, and the plan's own Rollback/Contingency section explicitly sanctions closing Phase 5 anyway while leaving Phase 4 partial. deploy-headless.sh ran clean (RESULT=landed_verify_clean) so every edited script is live in the deployed tree.

blockers.description: Phase 4's probe-artifact regeneration (measure-gate-costs.sh --regen-hints --skip-gate-measure, then measure-gate-costs.sh) requires a 1-minute host load average at or below 2.0 throughout the measurement window. Load was 1.49-1.77 at this phase's start but rose to 3.26-3.86 (confirmed via ps: a concurrent Lean build at 486% CPU, a Sapience hook at 99.6% CPU, multiple other active sessions) before the regeneration tasks could run. Resumable once the host is confirmed idle -- see the Phase 4 handoff for the exact resume commands.
